visuals.heading: What the Law Gives

blocks.heading: Career Options for Students
rows: Who is covered
The Act lists 21 specified disabilities. A benchmark disability means not less than 40 percent of a specified disability, certified by a certifying authority (Section 2(r)).
Reservations and most scholarships start at 40 percent. Below 40 percent you can still get exam help if writing is hard (see the exam section).
School years
Section 31: every child with a benchmark disability aged six to eighteen has the right to free education in a neighbourhood school or a special school of choice.
Ask the school for admission and support in writing, and keep a copy.
College seats
Admission also carries an upper age relaxation of five years.
The section names government and aided institutions. For a private unaided college, read its own prospectus; do not assume the 5 percent applies.
Government jobs

Section 34: every government establishment must fill not less than four percent of vacancies with persons with benchmark disabilities, in the posts identified for each disability. One percent each goes to blindness and low vision; deaf and hard of hearing; and locomotor disability (including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy). One percent goes to autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability, mental illness and multiple disabilities together.
The law sets a floor, not a job. Each recruitment notice lists which posts are identified for which disability, and a post can be closed to your category.
Land and schemes

Section 37 tells governments to make schemes with five percent reservation in allotment of land and housing, in poverty alleviation schemes, and in concessional land for setting up a business or enterprise.
This depends on schemes your state notifies. Ask your district office whether one is live before you plan around it.

blocks.heading: Extra Time and Language Relief
rows: CBSE (school boards)

Extra time of 20 minutes per hour: 60 minutes for a 3-hour paper, 50 for 2.5 hours, 40 for 2 hours, 30 for 1.5 hours. A scribe, free of cost, paid by the Board. Visually impaired candidates can use approved screen-reading software. Language exemptions for hearing, speech, visual and dyslexic candidates: in Class VI to VIII a third language is exempt, and in Class X one compulsory language can replace two. Exam and registration fees are waived for visually impaired students.

From the CBSE circular of 24 January 2017. Boards revise circulars, so confirm the current one with your school. Calculator rules differ between CBSE documents, so ask your school which applies in your exam year.
Government-conducted written exams (entrance and recruitment)
A scribe you bring should be one level below your own qualification. A scribe the exam body provides must not be above the exam's minimum qualification, and always matriculate or above.
Candidates with 40 percent or more fall under separate DEPwD guidelines dated 29 August 2018. Each exam bulletin says exactly how to apply, so read it on the day it opens.

blocks.heading: Scholarships and Fee Support
rows: Pre-matric (Classes IX and X)
Regular full-time student in a government or recognised school, benchmark disability, family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year.

25,000 slots a year. Maintenance allowance Rs 500 a month for day scholars and Rs 800 for hostellers, a book grant of Rs 1,000 a year, and a disability allowance of Rs 4,000 a year for visual and intellectual disabilities or Rs 2,000 for others.
Post-matric (Class XI to postgraduate)

17,000 slots a year. Maintenance from Rs 550 to Rs 1,600 a month depending on the course group and whether you live in a hostel, a book allowance of Rs 1,500 a year, the same disability allowance, and reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable fees up to Rs 1.5 lakh a year.
Top class education

300 slots. Tuition and non-refundable charges up to Rs 2 lakh a year, maintenance of Rs 3,000 a month for hostellers or Rs 1,500 for day scholars, Rs 2,000 a month for a reader or escort, Rs 5,000 a year for books, Rs 45,000 once for a laptop and Rs 30,000 once for assistive devices. One-time award, limited to the listed institutes.

blocks.heading: Match the Route to the Need
rows: Blindness and low vision
A screen reader (NVDA is free for Windows), enlarged print or e-text, a reader or scribe, papers without visual input.
Data and software work with a screen reader, teaching, counselling, law, writing and audio work.
Whether the tools your track needs (spreadsheets, design apps, code editors) work with your screen reader, before you pay for a course.
Captions, written instructions, a sign language interpreter, chat-based interviews. In school boards, the third-language exemption.

Design, data, software, accounts, research and writing. Sign-language work is its own career: the ISLRTC diploma in Indian Sign Language interpretation is a 2-year course, RCI approved, with an intake of 90 seats on its 2023-24 page.
Whether the workplace uses calls or open-plan meetings for core tasks, and whether the interview can be written or on video with captions.
Accessible campus and exam centre, a scribe if writing is hard, remote or hybrid work.
Most desk-based and remote tracks, teaching, accounts, law, design, data and software.
Ramps, lifts, toilets and the exam centre floor, in writing, before you pay a fee. The Act asks government-funded institutions to make campuses accessible.
Specific learning disability, autism, intellectual disability, mental illness
Extra time, a scribe or reader, written instructions, predictable routines and a quiet setting.
Choose by task, not stereotype. Written-brief, structured work such as testing, data, design, accounts and craft fits many people, but it is a starting point, not a rule.
Ask what is in writing: the accommodations in the offer letter, and whether interviews are timed. Dyslexia and other learning differences have their own exam rules, so read the bulletin of each exam.
Chronic neurological conditions and blood disorders (such as multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's, haemophilia, thalassemia, sickle cell disease)
Flexible hours, remote work, rest breaks, and attendance rules that allow treatment.
Remote and hybrid knowledge work, online teaching, writing, design, analysis.
Attendance rules in the course and workplace. Field-heavy and long-shift tracks need an honest energy check first.
Multiple disabilities, including deaf-blindness
Support is built around the person. Tactile communication, assistive technology and a trained helper may be needed.
Work with your doctor, a disability organisation and your family to match tasks to your communication method.

blocks.heading: Routes That Filter You Twice
rows: Government jobs
The written exam rank, within the reserved vacancies for your category.
Document and medical verification, and the check that the post is identified for your disability.
MBBS
A NEET UG score high enough for a seat in the reserved quota.
The Medical Assessment Board's Eligibility Certificate in counselling, under NMC's July 2026 guidelines. Later, a specialist seat is a third competition.
UPSC civil services
Prelims, Mains and Interview, in order.
Law practice
A seat in an entrance-based law degree.
Years of building a name before income steadies. Admission is not income.

blocks.heading: Career Options for Students
rows: Data and software
Employers, then project clients.
Portfolio, referral, a short note on how you work.
Write a two-line description of the problem you solve and for whom.
Accessibility testing
Companies that build sites and apps, agencies, public bodies.
Audit reports and a developer or designer who used them.
Turn one audit into a one-page before-and-after, then ask for one referral.
Teaching and tutoring
Schools and colleges, ed-tech firms, families.
Sample lessons, student results, parent reviews.
Offer one free trial session, then a clear monthly price.
Counselling and special education
Schools, hospitals, NGOs, families.
A recognised qualification and word of mouth from doctors and schools.
Explain your service in plain words to a parent in two sentences.
Design and writing
Agencies, brands, direct clients.
Portfolio, referral, a niche name.
Package one deliverable at one price, and follow up once.
Own business
Customers.
Reviews, repeat orders, a listing you own.
Have one honest price conversation, in writing, before work starts.

blocks.heading: College Money and the 10 Percent Rule

figures.label: Education Budget Example
figures.source: Our strongest suggestion: spend about 10 percent of the family's whole education budget on college fees.

figures.label: Education Budget Example
figures.source: On a 10 lakh rupee budget that is about 1 lakh rupees for the degree, and the other 9 lakh rupees must cover living costs, devices, internet, short courses, projects and future learning. Above about 20 percent, ask for hard evidence that the college gives something you cannot get otherwise, such as a licence your route legally needs. Borrow for a degree only when a legally required credential leaves no other way.

figures.label: Family Income Eligibility
figures.source: Family income limits are ₹2.5 lakh a year for pre-matric and post-matric and ₹8 lakh for top class.

blocks.heading: Pay for a Course or Degree

figures.label: Education Budget Example
figures.source: An illustration, not a real fee: on a Rs 3 lakh education budget, a tenth is Rs 30,000 for the main course and a fifth is Rs 60,000. Spend the rest on tools, practice and a reserve.

items.text: NVDA is a free, open-source screen reader for Windows, so the cost of starting is low.
Captions and speech-to-text help in classes, meetings and interviews.
AI assistants can summarise long documents, draft a first version, and explain code or a formula, which saves hours for people who read or write slowly.
Remote and hybrid work widens the market beyond your city.
